rationale: Closed the child question's last stated gap by running the cluster scenario in both restart modes inside one experiment: the same cluster, stores, partition and repair phases, with the restarted node using Config.RestoreCommittedLogs in one run and not in the other. Local construction feedback shows the only difference the mode makes: with the feature on the restarted node reports the stale {A,B,C}, wins the two-voter partition while the other three voters elect their own leader, and applies a write of its own; with the feature off it reports {A,B,C,D,E}, no node leads the two-voter partition, the cluster has a single leader, and the restarted node applies no write at all. The comparisons are therefore declared per mode with separate admissions so the receipt carries the A/B rather than only the defect side.

scope.description: The five-node restart scenario (bootstrap {A,B,C}, committed applies, user snapshot on A, AddVoter D and E, graceful shutdown of A, partition {A,C} | {B,D,E}, restart of A, healing, repair by snapshot install) executed twice in one run: once restarting A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and once restarting it with the feature off, everything else identical, including that both runs stage the commit index during the first life by running with the feature enabled before the restart.
assumptions: Both runs use freshly created stores and transports; the mode is the only intended difference, and in both runs A's first life runs with the feature enabled so a persisted commit index exists.
The partition, healing and repair phases run identically in both modes; the repair phase triggers a snapshot install in both runs because the leader compacts while the restarted node is cut off.

Recorded rather than asserted: the applied-write metric across nodes is only meaningful when both sides committed a write, so the control comparisons use the restarted node's own applied writes and the leader counts instead of cluster-wide consistency.
excluded: No crash, on-disk store or user Restore is exercised.
The control reproduces the same first-life and partition schedule; it is a control for the restart mode, not for the scenario.

experiment.prefix: The helper builds five InmemTransports in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore and Config with TrailingLogs 0, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and the feature enabled, waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A; it starts D and E, adds each as voter, applies one further command and emits 'fixture' (snapshot index and membership, newest configuration entry index and membership, stored commit index, pre-restart configuration and the derived operands). It shuts A down, cuts {A,C} from {B,D,E}, reconnects A to C only, restarts A from the same stores with the mode's restart feature setting and emits 'restart'. It waits for a leader in each partition, submits one Apply to each leader, reads both leaders' entries at the shared index and emits 'outcome' (leaders, terms, leader count, per-node leader booleans, reported configurations, write errors and indexes, payloads, conflicting_commits). It reconnects the mesh, waits for one leader, applies one more entry, waits 300ms and emits 'healed' (payloads and terms at the conflict index, applied write lists, configurations). It then runs the repair phase: choose a current-configuration leader, cut A off, apply ten commands, snapshot the leader, reconnect A, wait for the snapshot install, wait 300ms and emit 'repaired'. The test runs mode defect_restart first and control_no_restore second, so the event order is fixture, restart, outcome, healed, repaired, fixture, restart, outcome, healed, repaired.
semantic_changes: The scenario body moved into a helper that takes the mode and the restart feature flag; the test now runs defect_restart (restart with the feature) and control_no_restore (restart without it) in one execution, emitting the same five events per mode.
Admissions and comparisons are declared per mode so the receipt shows the feature-on and feature-off runs side by side.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft configuration scan plus the RestoreCommittedLogs replay: this control isolates the restart's feature setting as the cause of the stale membership and the minority election, since everything else about the two runs is identical.

comparisons.description: Feature on: the restarted node should use the committed configuration entry in its own log.
Feature off control: the same restart without the replay should use the committed configuration.
Feature on: the two-voter partition should not be able to elect a leader.
Feature off control: the same partition should not elect a leader.
Feature off control: the cluster should have exactly one leader.
Feature on: the restarted node should not have applied a write of its own that the current configuration never accepted.
Feature off control: the restarted node should have applied nothing of its own.

experiment.revision_reason: Runs the same scenario twice, once with the restart using RestoreCommittedLogs and once as a control with the feature off at restart, and declares mode-conditioned comparisons for both; the scenario phases themselves are unchanged, and the earlier comparisons remain with their own receipts.
